p: בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה עַל פָּסוּק הַמַּלְאָךְ הַגּוֹאֵל אִיתָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר הִקִּישׁ גְּאוּלָּה לְפַרְנָסָה וּפַרְנָסָה לִגְאוּלָּה מַה גְּאוּלָּה כִּפְלַיִם אַף פַּרְנָסָה כִּפְלַיִם וּמַה פַּרְנָסָה בְּכָל יוֹם אַף גְּאוּלָּה בְּכָל יוֹם.

— Bereishit Rabbah, on “The angel who redeems,” teaches: Rabbi Eleazar said, Scripture compares redemption to sustenance and sustenance to redemption. Just as redemption is twofold, sustenance is also twofold; just as sustenance is daily, redemption is also daily.
וְהִנֵּה בְּוַדַּאי אֵין פֵּירוּשׁ גְּאוּלָּה עַל גְּאוּלָּה הָעֲתִידָה דְּאִם כֵּן אֵיךְ אָמַר שֶׁהוּא בְּכָל יוֹם אַךְ עִיקַּר הַגְּאוּלָּה מִמִּלְחֶמֶת וְשִׁעְבּוּד הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
— Certainly “redemption” here does not mean the future redemption; otherwise, how could it be daily? Rather, the essential redemption is from the warfare and enslavement of the evil inclination.
שֶׁמִּזֶּה מִסְתָּעֵף כָּל הַקִּטְרוּגִים שֶׁאַף בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְצָא מֵהַקְּלִיפָּה שֶׁלָּהֶם.
— From this stem all accusations, since something of the nations’ impure husk is found even within Israel.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ דִּגְאוּלָּה בְּכָל יוֹם עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (סוּכָּה נב:) יִצְרוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו בְּכָל יוֹם וְכוּלֵי הַשֵּׁם לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ וְהָא בְּהָא תַּלְיָא.
— Redemption is daily, as taught in Sukkah 52b: a person’s inclination overpowers him each day, and so forth, but “Hashem will not abandon him to its hand.” These matters depend on one another.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קיח:) שֶׁהַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת נִיצּוֹל מִשִּׁיעְבּוּד.
— Thus the Sages said (Shabbat 118b) that one who delights in Shabbat is rescued from subjugation.

וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב שׁוֹמֵר שַׁבָּת מֵחַלְּלוֹ וְשׁוֹמֵר יָדוֹ מֵעֲשׂוֹת כָּל רָע וְאִיתָא בַּמְּכִילְתָּא (בְּשַׁלַּח) הָא לָמַדְנוּ שֶׁכָּל מִי שֶׁמְּשַׁמֵּר אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת מְרוּחָק מִן הָעֲבֵירָה.

— It is written, “Who guards Shabbat against profaning it and guards his hand against doing any evil.” The Mekhilta, Beshalach, teaches: we thus learn that whoever observes Shabbat is distanced from transgression.
וּבִפְרִי עֵץ חַיִּים הַלָּשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּיצּוֹל מִקִּטְרוּג הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וְנִיצּוֹל מִמֵּילָא מִשִּׁיעְבּוּד.
— In Pri Etz Chaim, the wording is that he is rescued from the evil inclination’s accusation and consequently from subjugation.

וְנִדְרָשׁ בַּגְּמָרָא מִדִּכְתִיב וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ וְגוֹמֵר וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פח ב) אִיתָא שֶׁבִּסְעוּדַת לֵיל שַׁבָּת כְּתִיב וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ וְגוֹמֵר וְהַיְינוּ דִּסְעוּדַת לֵיל שַׁבָּת חָשַׁב רַבִּי יִצְחָק לוּרְיָא זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.

— The Gemara derives this from “I will cause you to ride,” and so forth. The holy Zohar (II 88b) applies this verse to the Friday-night meal; the Ari, of blessed memory, correspondingly associated that meal with the holiness of our patriarch Isaac, peace be upon him.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז זוֹכִין לְמִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה פַּחַד יִצְחָק וְעַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁנִּכְנַס הַפַּחַד וְהַיִּרְאָה בַּלֵּב זוֹכִין לְהוֹרִיק הָרָע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ.
— Then one merits the attribute of awe, the Fear of Isaac. Through fear and awe entering the heart, one merits to empty evil from the fool’s heart at his left.

וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִיצּוֹל מִשִּׁיעְבּוּד וְאַף שֶׁהָעוֹלָם נִידּוֹן אַחַר רוּבּוֹ כְּבָר אָמַרְנוּ עַל מַה דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא שָׁם שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת נִיצּוֹל מֵחֶבְלוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין מַה הֲוֵי עֲלַיְיהוּ שֶׁקִּיְּימוּ הַשָּׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת וּכְבָר עָבַר כַּמָּה דּוֹרוֹת וְלֹא הָיוּ בִּזְמַן מָשִׁיחַ.

— Through this he is rescued from subjugation. Although the world is judged according to its majority, we have already discussed the Gemara’s statement there that the three Shabbat meals rescue one from the birth pangs of the Messiah. What becomes of those who observed these meals in generations long past, who did not live in the messianic period?

אַךְ כָּל נֶפֶשׁ בִּפְרָט נִיצּוֹל מֵחֶבְלוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל דּוֹר (וְנִתְבָּאֵר וַיֵּשֶׁב מַאֲמָר ה) וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ מַה פַּרְנָסָה בְּכָל יוֹם שֶׁצָּרִיךְ בְּכָל יוֹם לְפַרְנָסַת יוֹמוֹ.

— Rather, each individual soul is rescued from the messianic birth pangs that exist in every generation (as explained in Vayeshev, discourse 5). This is the meaning of “just as sustenance is daily”: each day requires that day’s sustenance.
אַף גְּאוּלָּה בְּכָל יוֹם הַגְּאוּלָּה מִקִּטְרוּג הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע גַּם כֵּן בְּכָל יוֹם.
— So redemption is daily too: redemption from the evil inclination’s accusation likewise occurs each day.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 97:3: ““The angel who redeems me from all evil.” Rabbi Yosei bar Chalafta said: Earning a livelihood is twice as hard as childbirth. Of childbirth it is written, “In pain you shall bear children”; of livelihood, “In toil you shall eat from it all the days of your life.” Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman differed. Rabbi Elazar said: Scripture links redemption with livelihood and livelihood with redemption: just as redemption is twofold, livelihood is twofold; just as livelihood is needed every day, redemption is needed every day. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said: Livelihood is greater than redemption, for redemption is through an angel, while livelihood comes through the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself. Redemption is through an angel: “The angel who redeems me.” Livelihood is through the Holy One, blessed be He: “You open Your hand and satisfy every living thing.” Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: A person’s sustenance is as difficult as the splitting of the Sea of Reeds, as it says, “Who divided the Sea of Reeds into parts,” and it says there, “Who gives bread to all flesh.””

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 88b: “Rabbi Shimon said: Whoever completes the three meals on Shabbat, a voice goes forth and proclaims concerning him: “Then you shall delight in Hashem”—this is one meal, corresponding to the Holy Ancient One, holiest of all. “I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth”—this is the second meal, corresponding to the field of holy apples. “I will feed you the inheritance of your father Jacob”—this is the completion fulfilled in Zeir Anpin. In correspondence with them a person must complete his meals, delight in all the meals, and rejoice in each one, for this is complete faith. Therefore Shabbat is more honored than all other appointed times and festivals: everything is found in it, which is not so of all the appointed times and festivals. Rabbi Chiyya said: Because everything is found in it, Shabbat is mentioned three times: “God completed on the seventh day”; “He rested on the seventh day”; “God blessed the seventh day.””

p: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ מַה גְּאוּלָּה כִּפְלַיִם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (רל א) דְּמַלְאָךְ הַגּוֹאֵל הוּא הַשְּׁכִינָה.
— “Just as redemption is twofold”: the holy Zohar (230a) explains that “the angel who redeems” is the Shekhinah.
וּבְפָרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח (נא א) עַיֵּן שָׁם בַּאֲרִיכוּת.
— See also its extended explanation in Beshalach, 51a.
וּמִלְּבַד הַהַצָּלָה מֵרָע הִנֵּה הִיא עוֹד מְאִירָה בְּתוֹסֶפֶת חַיִּים וּקְדוּשָּׁה בַּלֵּב.
— Besides rescuing from evil, She also shines additional life and holiness into the heart.
וְכֵן הַפַּרְנָסָה עִיקָּרָהּ דְּעַל מוֹצָא פִי הַשֵּׁם שֶׁבַּמַּאֲכָל יִחְיֶה הָאָדָם.
— Likewise, the essence of sustenance is that a person lives through the utterance of Hashem’s mouth contained within the food.
בְּתוֹסֶפֶת חַיּוּת וּקְדוּשָּׁה כְּשֶׁהָאֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה דְּעַל זֶה בָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צוֹרֶךְ הַמָּזוֹן.
— When one eats in holiness, vitality and holiness are increased; for this purpose Hashem created the need for food.
וְהִיא מַצֶּלֶת גַּם מֵרָע כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וּבֵרַךְ אֶת לַחְמְךָ וְגוֹמֵר וַהֲסִירוֹתִי מַחֲלָה מִקִּרְבֶּךָ.
— It also rescues from evil, as it says, “He will bless your bread,” and so forth, “and I will remove illness from your midst.”
וְהַגְּאוּלָּה מֵרָע בְּעַצְמוֹ הוּא גַּם כֵּן כִּפְלַיִם דִּכְתִיב הַמַּלְאָךְ הַגּוֹאֵל אוֹתִי מִכָּל רָע.
— Redemption from evil itself is also twofold, as it says, “The angel who redeems me from all evil.”

וְהִנֵּה הַקַּדְמוֹנִים כָּתְבוּ דִּלְשׁוֹן כֹּל הוּא לְפָחוֹת עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת כְּתוּבּוֹת ח. סוֹף דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל שֶׁהַכֹּל) וּבֶאֱמֶת מָצִינוּ בְּכַמָּה פְּסוּקִים וּמִשְׁנָיוֹת וּגְמָרָא לְשׁוֹן כֹּל אַף עַל שְׁנַיִם.

— The early authorities wrote that “all” applies to at least three (as Tosafot state, Ketubbot 8a, end of the comment beginning Shehakol). Yet in many verses, mishnayot, and talmudic passages, we find “all” applied even to two.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מָצִינוּ גַּם כֵּן בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה צ) עַל פָּסוּק וַיְהִי רָעָב בְּכָל הָאֲרָצוֹת בְּשָׁלֹשׁ אֲרָצוֹת בְּפַנְקְיָא וּבַעֲרַבְיָא וּבִפְלַסְטִינִי.
— Nevertheless, the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah, end of chapter 90) interprets “There was famine in all the lands” as three lands: Phoenicia, Arabia, and Palestine.
נִרְאֶה שֶׁדִּיְּיקוּ מִלְּשׁוֹן כֹּל עַל שָׁלֹשׁ אֲרָצוֹת כְּדַעַת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים.
— It appears that they inferred three lands from the word “all,” following the early authorities’ view.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 230a: “He began: “The angel who redeems me from all evil.” This verse requires reflection. Why does it say “who redeems,” rather than “who redeemed”? Because he is constantly present with human beings and never departs from a righteous person. Come and see: “The angel who redeems me” is the Shekhinah, which accompanies a person continually and does not leave him when he keeps the Torah’s commandments. Therefore a person must take care not to set out on a journey alone. What does “alone” mean? He should take care to keep the Torah’s commandments, so that the Shekhinah does not depart from him and he is forced to go alone, without the companionship of the Shekhinah.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 51a: “When the Matron travels, they all travel with her, as it is written: “The angel of God traveled.” Is she called “the angel of God”? Rabbi Abba said: Yes. Come and see: Rabbi Shimon said: The Holy One, blessed be He, established before Him a holy palace, a supernal palace, a holy city, a supernal city, called Jerusalem, the holy city. Whoever enters before the King enters only from that holy city, taking the path to the King, for the path is established from there. This is what is written: “This is the gate to Hashem; the righteous shall enter through it.” Every mission the King desires goes forth from the Matron’s house, and every mission from below to the King first enters the Matron’s house and proceeds from there to the King. Thus the Matron is the emissary for everything, from above to below and from below to above. Therefore she is the emissary for everything, as it is written: “The angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, traveled”—the Israel above. “The angel of God” is the one of whom it is written: “Hashem went before them,” “to travel by day and by night,” as we have explained.”

Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Vayechi 4:6: “According to what has been said, one can explain the words of the Midrash, ‘He compared sustenance to redemption: just as redemption is twofold, sustenance too is twofold.’ It is not understood what the ‘twofold’ is. But according to the above one may say: the first is the removal of the obstruction, the closing of mind and heart, and the second is the holy illuminations that come into the opened mind and heart, like ‘Remember’ and ‘Keep’ on Shabbat. This is ‘redemption is twofold, so too sustenance is twofold’: for the flow of sustenance there are two matters. The first is drawing the bounty from its source, and the second is that it reach the person; for many obstructions and accusers close the opening through which the bounty descends, and many judgments pass over that bounty after it leaves its source, and it matters how it descends, in a very coarse material garment or a fine one, and how much of ‘what comes from the mouth of Hashem’ is in it, as is known from the books. So just as redemption has two matters, removal of the obstruction and the giving, so sustenance has two matters, the giving and removal of the obstruction; the only difference between them is that in redemption removal of the obstruction comes first, and in sustenance the giving comes first and afterward removal of the obstruction.”

p: וְנִרְאֶה דְּבֶאֱמֶת כֹּל הוּא שָׁלֹשׁ וְהַיְינוּ שְׁנֵי קְצָווֹת וְהָאֶמְצָעִי הַכּוֹלְלָם וְכָךְ הוּא הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן תָּמִיד בִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
— It appears that “all” does indeed denote three: two extremes and the middle that encompasses them. This is always the pattern of enumeration within holiness.
וְכָךְ הוּא זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה בַּקְּלִיפָּה דִּשְׁלֹשׁ מִדּוֹת דְּרַע הַיְּדוּעוֹת קִנְאָה תַּאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד שֶׁהֵם שְׁלֹשָׁה רָאשֵׁי הָעֲבֵירוֹת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה גִּלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים.

— The corresponding pattern exists in impurity: the three familiar evil traits, envy, desire, and the pursuit of honor, underlie the three principal transgressions—idolatry, forbidden sexual relations, and bloodshed.

דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בָּא עַל יְדֵי הַכָּבוֹד דִּכְשֶׁבָּא לְתַכְלִית הַכָּבוֹד כְּמוֹ בִּנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר שֶׁמָּלַךְ בַּכִּיפָּה אָמַר אֶעֱלֶה עַל בָּמֳתֵי עָב וְגוֹמֵר וְכֵן הֲסָתַת הַנָּחָשׁ הָיָה וִהְיִיתֶם כֵּאלֹהִים.

— Idolatry arises through honor: on attaining its summit, as Nebuchadnezzar did when ruling the entire world, one says, “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds,” and so forth. The serpent’s enticement likewise was, “You will be like God.”
וְהֵם נֶגֶד שְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת בִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
— These oppose the three patriarchs within holiness.
וּמֵאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק יָצָא פְּסוֹלֶת יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְעֵשָׂו שֶׁהֵם גִּלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים.
— From Abraham and Isaac emerged the dross represented by Ishmael and Esau, corresponding to forbidden sexual relations and bloodshed.
אֲבָל מִיַּעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עא) כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר דַּל עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְדַבֵּר.
— But Jacob embodies utter lowliness, as Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 71, teaches: wherever “lowly,” “poor,” or “needy” is stated, it speaks of Israel.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלְּכוּ וְגוֹמֵר הָאֱלֹהִים הָרוֹעֶה אוֹתִי וְגוֹמֵר כִּי הוּא יָדַע דְּהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמִמֶּנּוּ לֹא יָצָא פְּסוֹלֶת.
— Thus it says, “The God before whom they walked,” and so forth, followed by “the God who shepherds me,” and so forth: Jacob knew that everything came from Hashem, and no dross emerged from him.
וְהַגֵּיאוּת הוּא עֲנַף הַתַּאֲוָה אוֹ הַקִּנְאָה וְנִמְשָׁךְ מֵאֶחָד מֵאֵלֶּה.
— Pride is a branch of desire or envy and derives from one of them.
וְכֵן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּאִיתָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין סג:) דְּלֹא עָבְדוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶלָּא לְהַתִּיר לָהֶם עֲרָיוֹת בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא.
— The same applies to idolatry: Sanhedrin 63b teaches that Israel worshipped idols only to permit themselves forbidden sexual relations openly.
וּבְיָרָבְעָם אִיתָא (שָׁם קא:) גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ טְרָדַתּוּ מִן הָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי עַיֵּן שָׁם דְּעַל יְדֵי הַקִּנְאָה בָּא לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
— Concerning Jeroboam it says (ibid. 101b) that his arrogance drove him from the world, and so forth; see there how envy brought him to idolatry.
וְעַל כֵּן הֵם רַק שְׁנֵי מִינֵי רַע וּמִזֶּה נִסְתָּעֵף הַשְּׁלִישִׁי הַכּוֹלְלָם.
— Thus there are essentially only two kinds of evil, from which the third, encompassing them, branches forth.
וְנֶגֶד אֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה הַשִּׁילּוּחַ מִשְּׁלֹשׁ מַחֲנוֹת (וְיִתְבָּאֵר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר).
— Corresponding to these three are the exclusions from the three camps, as will be explained elsewhere.
וְכֵן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה קְדוּשַּׁת אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק בְּחִינַת חֶסֶד וּגְבוּרָה.
— Within holiness, Abraham’s and Isaac’s holiness likewise corresponds to Chesed and Gevurah, lovingkindness and restraint.

וְיַעֲקֹב הַכּוֹלֵל שְׁתֵּי הַקְּדוּשּׁוֹת וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סח) יַעֲקֹב חֶבֶל נַחֲלָתוֹ מַה הַחֶבֶל הַזֶּה פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁלֹשׁ אֵין מַפְקִיעִין אוֹתוֹ כָּךְ הָאָבוֹת אֵין פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה.

— Jacob encompasses both forms of holiness. Thus Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 68, expounds “Jacob is the cord of His inheritance”: just as a cord is not twisted from fewer than three strands, so the patriarchs number no fewer than three.
וְנִקְרָא יַעֲקֹב חֶבֶל נַחֲלָתוֹ שֶׁכּוֹלֵל קְדוּשַּׁת שְׁנֵיהֶם.
— Jacob is called “the cord of His inheritance” because he encompasses the holiness of both.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א קסג ב וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת) דְּיַעֲקֹב כְּלָלָא דַּאֲבָהָן.
— As the holy Zohar states (I 163b and elsewhere), Jacob is the comprehensive embodiment of the patriarchs.
וְכֵן הוּא בְּכָל הַמִּסְפָּרִים שְׁנֵי הֶפְכִיִּים וְאֶחָד הַכּוֹלֵל אוֹתָם.
— This is the pattern in all such enumerations: two opposites and one that encompasses them.
וְעַל כֵּן אֱמֶת הוּא דִּלְשׁוֹן כֹּל שַׁיָּיךְ עַל שְׁנַיִם שֶׁכּוֹלֵל שָׁלֹשׁ עִם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי הַכּוֹלְלָם.
— It is therefore true that “all” may apply to two, since these include three when the third that encompasses them is counted.

וְכֵן הֲסָתַת הַנָּחָשׁ הָיָה בְּתַאֲוָה וּרְצִיחָה שֶׁהֶאֱכִילָה לְכָל בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים וְנִסְתָּעֵף בְּקַיִן דְּזֶהוּ הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ מִשְּׁנֵי מִינֵי רַע וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵהֶם נִסְתָּעֵף הַשְּׁלִישִׁי הַכּוֹלְלָם.

— The serpent’s enticement likewise involved desire and murder, for she fed all living creatures; this developed further in Cain. These two kinds of evil are the root, and afterward the third, encompassing them, branched forth from them.

וּלְעוּמַּת זֶה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה כְּשֶׁבָּא יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה כָּלוּל מִשְּׁתֵּי הַקְּדוּשּׁוֹת דְּאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק שׁוּב לֹא יָצָא מִמֶּנּוּ שׁוּם פְּסוֹלֶת וְהָיָה מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה.
— Correspondingly, within holiness, when our patriarch Jacob came, encompassing the two forms of holiness of Abraham and Isaac, no dross emerged from him, and his offspring were wholly faithful.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר הַמַּלְאָךְ הַגּוֹאֵל אוֹתִי מִכָּל רָע מִשְּׁתֵּי הַמִּדּוֹת בַּקְּלִיפָּה שֶׁהוּא כָּל רָע וּמִמֵּילָא נִיצּוֹל גַּם מֵהַשְּׁלִישִׁי.
— Thus, “The angel who redeems me from all evil” means from the two attributes of impurity that constitute all evil; consequently, one is rescued from the third as well.
וְזֶהוּ מַה גְּאוּלָּה כִּפְלַיִם שֶׁהוּא שְׁנֵי מִינֵי הָרַע שֶׁהוּא כָּל רָע שְׁנֵי הַהֶפְכִיִּים וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁי הַכּוֹלְלָם כָּאָמוּר.
— This is “just as redemption is twofold”: it concerns the two kinds of evil that constitute all evil, the two opposites and the third that encompasses them, as explained.

p: אַף פַּרְנָסָה כִּפְלַיִם
— “Sustenance too is twofold.”
שֶׁעִיקַּר הֲסָתַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִתּוֹךְ אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ הִשָּׁמְרוּ לָכֶם וְגוֹמֵר
— The evil inclination’s principal enticement arises from eating and drinking, as in “You shall eat and be satisfied,” followed by “Guard yourselves,” and so forth.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב עַל זֶה בַּסִּפְרֵי מִכַּמָּה פְּסוּקִים וְכֵן הוּא בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת לב.)
— Sifrei derives this from several verses, and Berakhot 32a teaches similarly.
וְאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יב:) קוֹדֶם שֶׁיֹּאכַל וְיִשְׁתֶּה יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי לְבָבוֹת לְאַחַר שֶׁאוֹכֵל וְשׁוֹתֶה אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא לֵב אֶחָד
— The Sages said (Bava Batra 12b): before eating and drinking, a person has two hearts; afterward, only one.
וְהַשְּׁתֵּי לְבָבוֹת שֶׁקּוֹדֶם שֶׁיֹּאכַל הֵם יֵצֶר טוֹב וְיֵצֶר הָרָע כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרָשׁ בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ.
— The two hearts before eating are the good and evil inclinations, as expounded on “with all your heart.”
וּלְאַחַר שֶׁיִּשְׁתֶּה לֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ אֵיזֶהוּ לֵב אֶחָד.
— It is not specified which single heart remains after drinking.
וְאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁתָּלוּי כְּפִי שֶׁהָיָה הָאֲכִילָה כְּשֶׁהַמְכוּוָּן לְמַלֵּא כְרֵסוֹ מֵבִיא קִטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרָע.
— We have explained that this depends on how one ate: when the intention is to fill the belly, it brings the evil inclination’s accusation.
וּכְשֶׁהָאֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה מֵבִיא שֶׁמְּתַקֵּן גַּם הַלֵּב כְּסִיל וְלוֹ לֵב אֶחָד לְאָבִיו שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם
— When eating is holy, however, it rectifies even the foolish heart, leaving one heart devoted to one’s Father in heaven.
וְהָאֲכִילָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְלַחְמִי וְגוֹמֵר
— Such eating accords with “Come, eat of My bread,” and so forth.
וְזֶהוּ אַף פַּרְנָסָה כִּפְלַיִם כְּשֶׁהוּא מִיַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
— This is “sustenance too is twofold”: when it comes from Hashem’s hand,
לֹא לְבַד שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵבִיא לִידֵי קִטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרָע
— it not only avoids provoking the evil inclination’s accusation,
רַק מַכְנִיס עוֹד קְדוּשָּׁה בְּלֵב חָכָם לִימִינוֹ שֶׁזּוֹכֶה עַל יְדֵי הָאֲכִילָה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ:
— but brings further holiness into the wise heart at one’s right, so that eating itself leads to words of Torah, as we have explained.

p: וְאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה לְעֵיל מִינָּהּ קָשָׁה הַפַּרְנָסָה כִּפְלַיִם כַּלֵּידָה.
— Earlier in Bereishit Rabbah, the Sages said that obtaining sustenance is twice as difficult as childbirth.

בְּלֵידָה כָּתוּב בְּעֶצֶב וְגוֹמֵר בְּפַרְנָסָה כְּתִיב בְּעִצָּבוֹן תֹּאכֲלֶנָּה וְכֵן הוּא בַּגְּמָרָא (פְּסָחִים קיח.) וְאַף דִּבְכָל מָקוֹם נוּ״ן מַקְטִין כְּמוֹ אִישׁוֹן בַּת עָיִן שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַקַּדְמוֹנִים שֶׁנִּקְרָא אִישׁוֹן מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה בָּעַיִן כִּדְמוּת אִישׁ קָטָן.

— Concerning childbirth it says “in pain,” and so forth; concerning sustenance, “in toil you shall eat of it.” Pesachim 118a likewise teaches this. Yet elsewhere a final nun is diminutive, as in ishon, “the pupil of the eye”: the early authorities explain that it is called ishon because the image of a little person appears in the eye.
וְכָאן נִדְרָשׁ בְּעִצָּבוֹן עַל לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים.
— Here, however, be’itzavon is expounded as denoting plurality.
אַךְ שְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת דְּעִנְיַן עֶצֶב שֶׁבַּלֵּידָה הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁשּׁוֹלֵחַ לָהּ יִסּוּרִין עַל יְדֵי הַקְּלָלָה אֲבָל הָאִשָּׁה מִצִּדָּהּ אֵין לָהּ עֶצֶב וְיִסּוּרִין.
— Both are true. The pain of childbirth comes from Hashem, who sends her suffering through the curse; the woman herself does not generate the pain and suffering.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּפַרְנָסָה שֶׁהָאָדָם יֵשׁ לוֹ עֶצֶב מֵעַצְמוֹ מַה שֶּׁהוֹמֶה וּמְהַמֶּה אַחַר הַשָּׂגַת פַּרְנָסָתוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּזֵיעַת אַפֶּךָ תֹּאכַל לֶחֶם.
— With sustenance, by contrast, a person produces distress himself through his agitation and turmoil in pursuing a livelihood, as it says, “By the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread.”

וְהַבּוֹטֵחַ בַּהַשֵּׁם מַמְצִיא לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פַּרְנָסָתוֹ בְּנַחַת וּכְתִיב שָׁטוּ הָעָם וְגוֹמֵר וְאָמַר (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב סב סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) שְׁטוּתָא הֲווֹ נָסְבֵי לְגַרְמַיְיהוּ בְּגִין דְּלָא הֲווֹ בְּנֵי מְהֵימְנוּתָא.

— Hashem provides a livelihood calmly for one who trusts in Him. It is written, “The people roamed about,” and so forth; the Zohar (II 62b, end) says that they took foolishness upon themselves because they were not people of faith.
וְלָכֵן כְּתִיב בְּעִצָּבוֹן בְּנוּ״ן הַקִּיטּוּן שֶׁהָעֶצֶב עִיקָּרוֹ מִצַּד הָאָדָם וְהוּא קָטָן.
— Thus be’itzavon is written with the diminutive nun: the distress principally arises from the person and is therefore small.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא עִצָּבוֹן לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים גַּם כֵּן שֶׁהוּא כִּפְלַיִם שֶׁהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הוּא גַּם מִקִּלְלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּזֵיעַת אַפֶּךָ וְגוֹמֵר.
— Nevertheless, it also denotes plurality and is twofold, since its root also lies in Hashem’s curse, “By the sweat of your brow,” and so forth.
וְכֵן אִישׁוֹן גַּם כֵּן מֵהַאי טַעֲמָא נִקְרָא בְּנוּ״ן הַקִּיטּוּן שֶׁהוּא רַק מִצַּד הָאָדָם הַמַּבִּיט בָּעַיִן וְרוֹאֶה כִּדְמוּת אִישׁ וְאֵינוֹ אִישׁ.
— For the same reason, ishon too takes the diminutive nun: it exists only from the perspective of the person looking into an eye and seeing a human likeness, though it is not a person.
וְכֵן עִצָּבוֹן הוּא מִצַּד הָאָדָם וְעַל כֵּן הוּא בְּנוּ״ן.
— Likewise, itzavon arises from the person, and therefore has a nun.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא כִּפְלַיִם שֶׁהוּא גַּם מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵהַקְּלָלָה וְגַם מִצַּד הָאָדָם.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 97:3: ““The angel who redeems me from all evil.” Rabbi Yosei bar Chalafta said: Earning a livelihood is twice as hard as childbirth. Of childbirth it is written, “In pain you shall bear children”; of livelihood, “In toil you shall eat from it all the days of your life.” Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman differed. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said: Livelihood is greater than redemption, for redemption is through an angel, while livelihood comes through the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself.
